_comment: Per-tool MCP enrichments. Applied on top of the OpenAPI-derived schema at registration time. Covers MCP-transport-specific limitations and cross-tool references not meaningful to plain REST callers.

aiagents_upload_knowledge_base.description_suffix: Pass each file as `{"name": "manual.pdf", "content_base64": "..."}` where `content_base64` is the file content base64-encoded (a raw base64 string or a `data:<mime>;base64,...` data URI both work). Max 50 MB per file. Allowed extensions: pdf, txt, json, csv, xml, md.

scenarios_run_voice.description_suffix:
There is no mode parameter — each run tool drives one transport, and the agent must have that connection configured (voice needs `telephony.phone_number`). Check configured connections via `aiagents_retrieve` before picking a run tool.

Dashboard link — the response `id` is a result id; view the run's results at `https://dashboard.cekura.ai/<project_id>/results/<id>`, where `<project_id>` is the project you are operating in. Surface this link when reporting the run to the user.

scenarios_run_text.description_suffix:
There is no mode parameter — each run tool drives one transport, and the agent must have that connection configured (text needs `provider.chat_agent_details`, or a websocket URL for self_hosted). Check via `aiagents_retrieve`. DO NOT USE for voice-specific metrics (latency, pitch) — they will be zero.

Dashboard link — the response `id` is a result id; view the run's results at `https://dashboard.cekura.ai/<project_id>/results/<id>`, where `<project_id>` is the project you are operating in. Surface this link when reporting the run to the user.

scenarios_run_pipecat_v1.description_suffix:
Requires a Pipecat API key configured on the project; each scenario carries its own room URL. Unsure this is the right run tool? Check the agent's configured connections via `aiagents_retrieve`.

Dashboard link — the response `id` is a result id; view the run's results at `https://dashboard.cekura.ai/<project_id>/results/<id>`, where `<project_id>` is the project you are operating in. Surface this link when reporting the run to the user.

scenarios_run_websocket.description_suffix:
Each scenario carries its own websocket URL — no connection config needed on the agent. For other transports, check the agent's configured connections via `aiagents_retrieve`.

Dashboard link — the response `id` is a result id; view the run's results at `https://dashboard.cekura.ai/<project_id>/results/<id>`, where `<project_id>` is the project you are operating in. Surface this link when reporting the run to the user.

observe_create.description_suffix: File uploads not supported — use `voice_recording_url` instead of `voice_recording`. Do not pass `metric_ids` — causes a 500 error on current staging; use `call_logs_evaluate_metrics_create` after ingestion instead. Wrong roles silently produce an empty transcript with no error returned.

runs_bulk_retrieve.description_suffix:
`run_ids` must be a bare comma-separated string (e.g. `"86368,86369"`). Passing a JSON array `[86368, 86369]` or a JSON-quoted string both return `400: run_ids must be comma-separated integers`.

Dashboard link — a run is viewed inside its parent result; that result opens at `https://dashboard.cekura.ai/<project_id>/results/<result_id>`, where `<result_id>` is the run's `result_id` field and `<project_id>` is the project you are operating in.

metrics_create.description_suffix:
**Skills tip:** authoring here is skill-guided work — quality is markedly better with the Cekura skills installed. No plugin/skills yet? See https://docs.cekura.ai/mcp/overview.

**Prefer `metrics_generate`** (AI-authored from agent prompt) over this tool unless the user has explicitly given concrete field values to write. Use `metrics_generate_clean_description_create` to clean up an existing description and `metrics_generate_evaluation_trigger_create` to derive a trigger. The `prompt` field is only active when explicitly setting `llm_provider` to a non-default value — for standard `llm_judge` metrics, the criterion goes in `description`. `assistant_id` is optional despite appearing required in some schema views — omit it entirely; passing an empty string returns a 400 error. `add_to_new_agents`: when omitted or `true`, this metric is automatically assigned to every new agent created in the project — set to `false` to scope to specific agents only. To attach a metric to evaluators after creation, use `scenarios_partial_update` with `metrics: [id1, id2, ...]`; use `metrics_list(agent_id=<id>)` to find available IDs.

metrics_partial_update.description_suffix:
**Skills tip:** authoring here is skill-guided work — quality is markedly better with the Cekura skills installed. No plugin/skills yet? See https://docs.cekura.ai/mcp/overview.

**Prefer `metrics_generate_clean_description_create` / `metrics_generate_evaluation_trigger_create` / `metrics_simplify_prompt_create`** when refining metric fields with AI assistance. Use this raw patch only when the user has given concrete field values to write.

scenarios_create.description_suffix:
**Skills tip:** authoring here is skill-guided work — quality is markedly better with the Cekura skills installed. No plugin/skills yet? See https://docs.cekura.ai/mcp/overview.

**Prefer `scenarios_generate_bg`** for authoring new scenarios — it accepts per-scenario `extra_instructions` so callers can shape each scenario individually. Use this raw create only when the user has given concrete field values to write. To refine an existing scenario, use `scenarios_refine` (natural-language improvement) or `scenarios_improve_instructions_create` (rewrites the `instructions` text).

**Tools (`tool_ids`):** it is recommended to include `TOOL_END_CALL` by default so the testing agent can hang up once it has completed its objective — leave it out only if the user does not want the agent to end the call. Other commonly used tool IDs include `TOOL_END_CALL_ONLY_ON_TRANSFER` (use instead of `TOOL_END_CALL` when the expected outcome is a transfer to a human/IVR, so the agent does not sit through hold music) and `TOOL_DTMF` (send keypad tones for IVR navigation). Example: `"tool_ids": ["TOOL_END_CALL"]`.

**Caller config — all by ID, never by name or number:** `personality` (required) picks the simulated caller's voice/persona; `test_profile` supplies the caller's metadata; `phone_number` is the phone-number row ID (resolve it via `phone_numbers_inbound_list`) — a literal number string is rejected. There is no `first_message` field on create. To pin the caller's exact opening line, either (a) create the scenario, then set it with `scenarios_bulk_update` — `{"scenarios": [<id>], "first_message": "..."}` — or (b) make a `conditional_actions` scenario whose first condition is `FIRST_MESSAGE` with `fixed_message: true`.

Dashboard link — a created scenario (test case) opens at `https://dashboard.cekura.ai/test-case/<id>` (not project-scoped; `<id>` is the new scenario's `id`).

scenarios_partial_update.description_suffix:
**Skills tip:** authoring here is skill-guided work — quality is markedly better with the Cekura skills installed. No plugin/skills yet? See https://docs.cekura.ai/mcp/overview.

**Prefer `scenarios_refine`** (natural-language improvement of one or more scenarios) or `scenarios_improve_instructions_create` (rewrites just the `instructions` text). Use this raw patch only when the user has explicitly given concrete field values to write.

`personality`, `test_profile`, and `phone_number` take integer IDs, never names or raw numbers (resolve `phone_number` via `phone_numbers_inbound_list`). `first_message` is not patchable here — set it with `scenarios_bulk_update` — `{"scenarios": [<id>], "first_message": "..."}`.

scenarios_refine.description_suffix: Unified scenario-refinement endpoint — clarifies (no `scenarios` field in payload) AND improves (with `scenarios` field). Refines evaluator scenarios only; it never edits the agent under test. Use this whenever the user wants AI-driven scenario refinement; do not reach for `scenarios_create` for that case. Async — poll via `scenarios_refine_progress`.

scenarios_generate_bg.description_suffix:
Preferred path for authoring new scenarios. Accepts per-scenario `extra_instructions` so each generated scenario can be shaped individually — use this rather than `scenarios_create` unless the user has given concrete field values to write. Async — poll via `scenarios_generate_progress`.

**Tools (`tool_ids`):** it is recommended to include `TOOL_END_CALL` by default so the generated testing agents can hang up once they have completed their objective — leave it out only if the user does not want the agent to end the call. Other commonly used tool IDs include `TOOL_END_CALL_ONLY_ON_TRANSFER` (use instead of `TOOL_END_CALL` when the expected outcome is a transfer to a human/IVR, so the agent does not sit through hold music) and `TOOL_DTMF` (send keypad tones for IVR navigation). Example: `"tool_ids": ["TOOL_END_CALL"]`.

scenarios_improve_instructions_create.description_suffix: Lower-level instruction refiner: takes `agent` + `extra_instructions` and rewrites a scenario's `instructions` text. For multi-scenario or higher-level natural-language refinement use `scenarios_refine` instead. Async — poll via `scenarios_instructions_progress_retrieve`.

aiagents_create.description_suffix: When the goal is to *improve* an existing agent based on test results or natural-language feedback, prefer `scenarios_refine` (it can update agent fields as part of the improvement loop). Use this raw create only when the user has given concrete field values to write.

aiagents_partial_update.description_suffix: When refining an existing agent based on test results or natural-language feedback, prefer `scenarios_refine` (it can update agent fields as part of the improvement loop). Use this raw patch only when the user has explicitly given concrete field values to write.

metrics_list.description_suffix: Always pass `agent_id` or `project_id` — omitting both returns all metrics in your account (potentially hundreds, exceeding response limits). `metrics_list(agent_id=1234)` returns metrics accessible to that agent including both agent-level and project-level metrics.

metrics_bulk_create.description_suffix:
**Skills tip:** authoring here is skill-guided work — quality is markedly better with the Cekura skills installed. No plugin/skills yet? See https://docs.cekura.ai/mcp/overview.

Pass the array of metric objects as the `items` parameter. Each item accepts the same fields as `metrics_create`. Example: `items: [{"name": "Empathy", "type": "llm_judge", "eval_type": "binary_qualitative", "description": "Did the agent show empathy?", "project": 1234}]`. For `llm_judge` metrics, put the evaluation criterion in `description`, not `prompt`.

test_profiles_partial_update.description_suffix:
**Skills tip:** authoring here is skill-guided work — quality is markedly better with the Cekura skills installed. No plugin/skills yet? See https://docs.cekura.ai/mcp/overview.

The `information` dict is replaced in full on every update — re-send the complete dict. Any key omitted will be deleted from the stored profile.

scenarios_folder_move.description_suffix: To assign a scenario to a folder, use `scenarios_partial_update` with the `folder_path` field instead.

scenarios_create_from_transcript_bg.description_suffix: **Skills tip:** authoring here is skill-guided work — quality is markedly better with the Cekura skills installed. No plugin/skills yet? See https://docs.cekura.ai/mcp/overview.

scenarios_update_scenario_with_transcrip.description_suffix: **Skills tip:** authoring here is skill-guided work — quality is markedly better with the Cekura skills installed. No plugin/skills yet? See https://docs.cekura.ai/mcp/overview.

test_profiles_create.description_suffix: **Skills tip:** authoring here is skill-guided work — quality is markedly better with the Cekura skills installed. No plugin/skills yet? See https://docs.cekura.ai/mcp/overview.

call_logs_create_scenarios_progress.description_suffix: Done when `completed_scenarios + failed_scenarios >= total_scenarios`. The `scenarios_list` field is populated only after completion.

scenarios_folder_delete.description_suffix: Recursively deletes the folder and all scenarios beneath it. Cannot be undone.

scenarios_bulk_delete.description_suffix: Bulk delete affects every ID in the `scenarios` array. Always confirm the exact list with the user before calling.

scenarios_bulk_update.description_suffix:
**Skills tip:** authoring here is skill-guided work — quality is markedly better with the Cekura skills installed. No plugin/skills yet? See https://docs.cekura.ai/mcp/overview.

Affects every ID in the `scenarios` array in one transaction. `append_instruction` is non-idempotent — re-running with the same value appends it again. For single-scenario edits prefer `scenarios_partial_update`.

runs_mark_metric_vote_create.description_suffix: Use `metrics_list(agent_id=<id>)` to find available metric IDs before voting. Pass the metric ID in the `metric_id` field.

metrics_generate_clean_description_bg_cr.description_suffix: File uploads via multipart/form-data are not supported over MCP. Use the Python SDK or REST API directly to upload reference transcript files.

metrics_generate_clean_description_progr.description_suffix: Poll this endpoint with the progress_id returned from metrics_generate_clean_description_bg_create. Status values: queued, processing, completed, failed. On completed, clean_description and thinking fields contain the result.

aiagents_destroy.description_suffix: Deletes the agent and all associated resources (scenarios, runs, results, call logs). Cannot be undone.

aiagents_duplicate_create.description_suffix: File uploads not supported via MCP. Use the Cekura dashboard or Python SDK for knowledge base file uploads. Call without file parameters to duplicate agent configuration only.

aiagents_update.description_suffix: File uploads not supported via MCP. Use the Cekura dashboard or Python SDK to upload knowledge base files. Updates without file parameters modify agent configuration only.

aiagents_auto_fetch_create.description_suffix: Async — returns a progress_id. Poll aiagents_auto_fetch_progress_retrieve with the progress_id until completed or failed.

aiagents_auto_fetch_progress_retrieve.description_suffix: Poll with the progress_id from aiagents_auto_fetch_create. Status values: queued, in_progress, completed (with staged configuration), failed (with error).

results_retrieve.description_suffix: Dashboard link — this result opens at `https://dashboard.cekura.ai/<project_id>/results/<id>`, where `<id>` is this result's `id` and `<project_id>` is the project you are operating in.

results_list.description_suffix: Dashboard link — each result opens at `https://dashboard.cekura.ai/<project_id>/results/<result_id>`, using the item's `id` and the project you are operating in.

scenarios_retrieve.description_suffix: Dashboard link — a scenario (test case) opens at `https://dashboard.cekura.ai/test-case/<id>` (not project-scoped; `<id>` is the scenario's `id`).

scenarios_list.description_suffix: Dashboard link — each scenario (test case) opens at `https://dashboard.cekura.ai/test-case/<id>` (not project-scoped; use the item's `id`).

metrics_generate_metrics_progress_retrie.description_suffix: Async — initiated by metrics_generate. Poll until status is completed or failed. Returns generated_metrics[] on completion.

metrics_simplify_prompt_progress_retriev.description_suffix: Async — initiated by metrics_simplify_prompt_create. Poll until status is completed or failed.

metrics_generate_clean_description_creat.description_suffix: Async — returns a progress_id. Poll `metrics_generate_clean_description_progress_retrieve` until status is completed or failed. On completion, `clean_description` and `thinking` fields contain the result.

metrics_generate_evaluation_trigger_crea.description_suffix: Async — returns a progress_id. Poll the corresponding metrics progress endpoint until status is completed or failed. Part of the metric authoring workflow; use after `metrics_create` to auto-generate the evaluation trigger condition.

metrics_generate.description_suffix: Async — returns a progress_id. Poll `metrics_generate_metrics_progress_retrieve` until status is completed or failed. Returns `generated_metrics[]` on completion. Prefer this over `metrics_create` unless the user has given concrete field values.

metrics_preview_create.description_suffix: Async — returns a progress_id. Poll `metrics_preview_progress` until status is completed or failed. Use to validate metric configuration before committing with `metrics_create` or `metrics_partial_update`.

metrics_run_reviews_create.description_suffix: Async — returns a progress_id. Poll `metrics_run_reviews_progress` until status is completed or failed. Evaluates recent runs against the metric and produces review entries.

metrics_simplify_prompt_create.description_suffix: Async — returns a progress_id. Poll `metrics_simplify_prompt_progress_retrieve` until status is completed or failed. Rewrites the metric prompt for clarity and conciseness.

scenarios_folder_create.description_suffix: Synchronous — returns the created folder immediately (unlike other `scenarios_*_create` endpoints which are async with progress polling). Use `scenarios_folders_list` to see existing folders before creating.

scenarios_generate_instructions_create.description_suffix: Async — returns a progress_id. Poll `scenarios_instructions_progress_retrieve` until status is completed or failed. Generates scenario instructions from agent context.

scenarios_generate_progress.description_suffix: Progress poller for `scenarios_generate_bg`. Poll until status is completed or failed. On completion, generated scenario IDs are available in the response.

personalities_fork_create.description_suffix: Copies settings only — it takes no field overrides beyond `prompt`, so follow it with `personalities_partial_update` on the returned id to change anything else. The fork is enabled for the target project automatically, and its `voice_id` is the real one (a globally available personality reports its `voice_id` as the placeholder `vocera_voice_id`, so forking is also how you get a predefined voice you can read and modify).

metric_failure_mode_insights_categories_.description_suffix: Async — reviews are created in Labs after a short delay. List categories via `metric_failure_mode_insights_categories_retrieve` to confirm processing completed.

metric_failure_mode_insights_fix_metric_.description_suffix: Async — reviews are created in Labs after a short delay. Retrieve the insight via `metric_failure_mode_insights_retrieve` to confirm processing completed.

call_logs_evaluate_metrics_create.description_suffix: Known issue: the `metrics` filter is not enforced — all metrics assigned to the call log are evaluated regardless of which IDs are passed.

call_logs_list.description_suffix:
Work narrow: isolate the calls you want with `filters_v2` (e.g. `{"field": "success", "op": "eq", "value": false}`) and a `timestamp_from`/`timestamp_to` window, request `page_size=5`, then walk pages with `page`. Use `ql` to keep each row to the fields you will actually read. If you already know the call, skip the list entirely and pull it by ID with `call_logs_retrieve`.

**Counting** — the response carries no total unless you ask for one: pass `include_count=true` (with `page_size=1` when the number is all you need) and read `count`. `count_capped: true` means the true total is above 10000. Never probe or walk pages just to count.

Dashboard link — each call log opens at `https://dashboard.cekura.ai/<project>/calls?callId=<id>`, using the item's `project` and `id` fields.

call_logs_mark_metric_vote_create.description_suffix: Use `metrics_list(agent_id=<id>)` to find available metric IDs before voting. Pass the metric ID in the `metric_id` field.

call_logs_retrieve.description_suffix: Dashboard link — this call log opens at `https://dashboard.cekura.ai/<project>/calls?callId=<id>`, using the response's `project` and `id` fields.

personalities_create.description_suffix:
**Skills tip:** authoring here is skill-guided work — quality is markedly better with the Cekura skills installed. No plugin/skills yet? See https://docs.cekura.ai/mcp/overview.

**Personality vs. evaluator — do not mix them.** A personality is the simulated caller's *voice layer*: voice and accent, language, speaking speed, interruption behavior, background noise and volume, idle timing, network impairment. An evaluator is the *test case* that caller runs — what it is trying to do, what it says, and what counts as success. A trait that lasts the whole call belongs on the personality; a thing that happens at one step belongs in the evaluator. Evaluator instructions cannot change any voice-layer setting: writing "speak with an Indian accent" or "interrupt constantly" into instructions has no effect on the audio, the run still passes, and the behavior never happens.

**Accent comes from the voice, not from a field.** Speech is synthesised from `voice_id` alone — nothing in the call pipeline reads the `accent` field, which is why it is read-only and absent from this tool's inputs. To test an accent, pick a voice that has it: call `personalities_elevenlabs_voices` (ElevenLabs publishes an accent label per voice) or `personalities_cartesia_voices`, both filterable by `language`, and pass the id you find as `voice_id` together with the matching `provider`. The stored `accent` label is then derived from that voice, so it always describes what the call actually sounds like.

**Send `voice_id` and `provider` together.** `provider` is what selects the catalog the voice id is looked up in; without it an invalid id can be stored unvalidated and the derived `accent` and `gender` are left blank. `voice_model` must belong to the same provider (`eleven_*` models with `11labs`, `sonic-3.5` with `cartesia`).

**Prefer forking over creating.** If a predefined personality is nearly right, `personalities_fork_create` copies every setting into your project and you patch only the difference — cheaper and less error-prone than rebuilding a voice config from scratch. Create from scratch when no predefined personality is close, or when the language has none.

Dashboard link — a created personality opens at `https://dashboard.cekura.ai/personality/edit/<id>` (not project-scoped; `<id>` is the new personality's `id`).

personalities_partial_update.description_suffix:
**Skills tip:** authoring here is skill-guided work — quality is markedly better with the Cekura skills installed. No plugin/skills yet? See https://docs.cekura.ai/mcp/overview.

**Personality vs. evaluator — do not mix them.** A personality is the simulated caller's *voice layer*: voice and accent, language, speaking speed, interruption behavior, background noise and volume, idle timing, network impairment. An evaluator is the *test case* that caller runs — what it is trying to do, what it says, and what counts as success. A trait that lasts the whole call belongs on the personality; a thing that happens at one step belongs in the evaluator. Evaluator instructions cannot change any voice-layer setting: writing "speak with an Indian accent" or "interrupt constantly" into instructions has no effect on the audio, the run still passes, and the behavior never happens.

**Accent comes from the voice, not from a field.** Speech is synthesised from `voice_id` alone — nothing in the call pipeline reads the `accent` field, which is why it is read-only and absent from this tool's inputs. To test an accent, pick a voice that has it: call `personalities_elevenlabs_voices` (ElevenLabs publishes an accent label per voice) or `personalities_cartesia_voices`, both filterable by `language`, and pass the id you find as `voice_id` together with the matching `provider`. The stored `accent` label is then derived from that voice, so it always describes what the call actually sounds like.

**This patch fans out.** Every evaluator already pointing at this personality picks up the change on its next run — there is no per-evaluator override. When the change should apply to only some evaluators, `personalities_fork_create` first and patch the fork.

Globally available personalities (no `project`/`organization` owner — every predefined one) cannot be patched at all; fork one into your project first.

personalities_list.description_suffix:
Heavy response — pass `language` (e.g. `en`, `es`) whenever you know the agent's language, and `project_id` to scope to a project's own personalities plus the globally available ones. Already know which personality you mean? Use `personalities_retrieve` instead.

Reading the results: `accent` is a label derived from the voice and is empty for voices whose provider publishes none (all Cartesia voices) — an empty `accent` does not mean the voice is accent-free. `voice_id` reads as the placeholder `vocera_voice_id` on globally available personalities; fork one to see and change its real voice.

personalities_elevenlabs_voices.description_suffix:
Read-only catalog lookup — it does not change a personality. Feed the id you pick to `personalities_create` or `personalities_partial_update` as `voice_id`, with the matching `provider`. This is the correct way to set a personality's accent: the accent is a property of the voice, and the `accent` field is a derived read-only label.

Each voice carries a `labels` object with ElevenLabs' own `accent`, `gender`, `age` and `use_case`, plus a `preview_url`. Match on `labels.accent` when the test targets a specific accent. Pair the chosen id with `provider: "11labs"` and an `eleven_*` `voice_model`.

personalities_cartesia_voices.description_suffix:
Read-only catalog lookup — it does not change a personality. Feed the id you pick to `personalities_create` or `personalities_partial_update` as `voice_id`, with the matching `provider`. This is the correct way to set a personality's accent: the accent is a property of the voice, and the `accent` field is a derived read-only label.

Cartesia publishes no accent label — each voice carries `language`, `gender`, a free-text `description` and `preview_file_url`, so accent has to be read out of the name and description. When a test needs a *named* accent, prefer `personalities_elevenlabs_voices`. Pair the chosen id with `provider: "cartesia"` and `voice_model: "sonic-3.5"`.
